messages:
maria: FYI rolling base-image bump with nvidia-container-toolkit v1.11 to eu-west gpu nodepool. After first wave, several pods report no GPUs and crashlooping. Anyone seen this? :confused:
jon: saw a couple of nodes show "Failed to load libnvidia-ml.so" in container logs earlier. Sounds like bind-mounts not propagating into cri.
yu: confirming, containerd nodes only. dockerd-hosts seem ok. kernel+driver versions look unchanged (510.60), toolkit is the only diff.
maria: exact error snippet from a failing pod: 
```
I0902 09:12:03.123456 1 main.cpp:45] initializing GPU runtime
E0902 09:12:03.124000 1 loader.cpp:88] dlopen failed: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```
infra-oncall: thanks, rolling back toolkit on one node to 1.10 now to test. Can you cordon a node for me?
jon: cordoned gpu-eu-west-07 and draining. Will repro by starting a test busybox image that binds /usr/lib from host.
devx: quick note — our base image bake added nvidia-toolkit via apt which created symlinks under /usr/local/nvidia and relies on host bind propagation. On containerd with private mount namespaces that can fail unless host mounts are rshared.
maria: interesting — does that mean the host's /usr/lib mount propagation setting changed in our new image?
yu: it's not the image, it's the toolkit package that uses a tmpfs overlay during install and leaves symlinks pointing to /var/lib/nvidia with private mounts. When we start containers, the symlink target isn't visible. We saw similar with toolkit 1.9 but fixed by setting --volume /usr/lib:/usr/lib:rshared at runtime.
jon: workaround tested: started gpu pod with hostMount + mountPropagation: HostToContainer and it sees GPUs. But we can't change every pod spec.
infra-oncall: TL;DR: immediate options:
- revert base-image/toolkit to 1.10 for eu-west nodepool (fast)
- patch daemonset installer to use bindPropagation rshared on kubelet/containerd mounts (need coord with infra teams)
- roll nodes through kernel+driver revalidate (risky)
maria: cost/impact: reverting costs node churn but minimal. If we evacuate eu-west to other regions to keep SLA, cross-region bandwidth and latency for jobs => extra egress and slower jobs. FYI billing showed 18% increase on inter-region traffic last time we did that.
devx: long-term fix: vendor the libcuda libs into our base image and ensure symlinks are absolute within the image (no host bind reliance). That eliminates reliance on mount propagation.
yu: created a short repro repo: https://git.internal/repro/nv-toolkit-bind-issue — shows containerd vs dockerd behaviour + mounting flags.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: rollback-toolkit-eu-west -> 3 nodes target (started)
jon: after rollback of one node to toolkit 1.10 the pod came up and saw GPUs again. So root cause confirmed.
maria: OK let's do staged rollback and immediate postmortem. I'll open a JIRA with remediation: pin toolkit in images, update daemonset to set HostToContainer where reasonable, and long-term vendor libs.
infra-oncall: note for the postmortem: include kubelet/containerd config, exact toolkit package versions, and kernel-driver mismatch checks. Also add a test in our node-image CI to run a minimal gpu visibility check after toolkit pkg installs.
devx: adding a sample kubectl snippet for debug and quick repro: 
```
kubectl run debug-gpu --rm -it --image=redwood/busybox:gpu --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"c","image":"redwood/busybox:gpu","volumeMounts":[{"mountPath":"/usr/lib","name":"hostlib","mountPropagation":"HostToContainer","readOnly":true}] }],"volumes":[{"name":"hostlib","hostPath":{"path":"/usr/lib"}}]}}' -- sleep 3600
```
maria: thanks. I'll coordinate rollback and update the status page. Keep posting any new nodes that fail in this thread. :thumbsup:
